research_analysis.exact_observed_hook: "This chocolate brand literally sold chocolate bars with a piece missing on purpose."
research_analysis.visual_hook: Stacked split screen. Top: hands tearing open a chocolate wrapper to show a bar with a corner missing, under a white header box reading "This is WILD marketing 🤯". Bottom: the presenter in a white shirt with a clip-on mic against a dark background.
research_analysis.narrative_structure: Fixed headline for the whole video. A brand does something that looks like a mistake, the public gets angry, 'then the twist hit', a result number, and a question to the audience at the end.
research_analysis.viral_mechanism: The top panel shows the 'mistake' as proof while the bottom panel tells the story, so the viewer never has to take the claim on trust. The mistake-anger-twist order is a three-act story in under 45 seconds.
research_analysis.observed_evidence: 2.7M views on a 3.6K-follower account, 433.8x its 6.2K median, 41s. Fixed header, word-by-word subtitles, campaign footage on top. Caption ends with a question to the viewer.
research_analysis.performance_hypothesis: Hypothesis: 'on purpose' plus visible evidence makes people watch for the twist, and the closing question produces comments naming a person or an opinion. A tiny account reaching 2.7M suggests the structure does the work.
research_analysis.why_this_format_fits_alex: He can be both the brand and the narrator: he runs the stunt on his own Trial Reel and reports the real result. That removes any unverified brand claim, shows a marketing experiment with his own numbers, and uses the Trial Reel workflow he already runs daily.
research_analysis.originality_changes: Borrowed: stacked split screen, fixed headline, mistake then reaction then twist then result then question. New: the campaign is his own deliberate typo, the evidence is his own comment section, and the result is whatever his Insights show, including a failure.

alex_adaptation.concept: Step one, before this video: he posts any silent Trial Reel from this package with 'Florida' spelled 'Flordia' in the on-screen text. Step two, 48 hours later: this split-screen video shows that Reel and its comments on top while he explains below that the typo was planted, and reports honestly whether corrections raised the comment count against his recent average.
alex_adaptation.target_audience: Creators and marketers curious about engagement tactics; viewers who enjoy being let in on a trick.
alex_adaptation.primary_emotion: Surprise at being shown the trick, then curiosity about the number
alex_adaptation.first_frame: Split screen. Top: his own Reel paused on the frame where the text reads 'Flordia', with a red circle around the word. Header: 'I did this on purpose'. Bottom: Alex chest-up with a clip-on mic.
alex_adaptation.first_spoken_line: Two days ago I posted a video where I spelled Florida wrong. On purpose.

production.editor_instructions: Prerequisite: post one silent Trial Reel with 'Flordia' in the text at least 48 hours before filming this, and note the comment counts of the previous five trials at their own 48-hour mark. Fill the {{REAL}} tokens only from Insights. Keep only the true outcome branch. Blur every commenter's username. Plant exactly one misspelled word in this video's subtitles for the ending. Five videos is a small sample: the script reports the numbers and does not claim the typo caused them.

variants_to_test: Alternate hook: 'I got corrected by strangers for 48 hours straight. That was the plan.'
Alternate payoff: 'Did you stay to see the number? Also yes.'
testing.promotion_decision: Brand fit 3: promote at 48h if views are at least 3x his trailing median and comments per 1,000 reached is top quartile; the typo Reel itself stays a trial and is not promoted.
follow_up_variations_if_successful: Same split-screen report on a different test: identical video posted with and without on-screen text
Report on a hook test: the same Reel with two different first lines, both numbers shown
Report on length: a 9-second and a 30-second cut of the same joke

creative_confidence.score_type: Subjective production-priority score, not predicted viral probability
creative_confidence.rationale: A real experiment with his own receipts and an ending that turns the viewer into a participant. It shows the agency's thinking with no client and no income claim. It needs a prior post, a 48-hour wait and a fiddly split-screen edit.
uncertainties: Result is unknown until the typo Reel runs; both branches are scripted and only the true one may be used
A five-video comparison cannot prove cause; the script avoids saying it does
Some viewers consider typo bait cheap; the script admits that rather than hiding it
Split-screen explainer is a new format for him
